articles.summary: Quentin Tarantino has long said he’ll be retiring after his 10th feature film, but fans shouldn’t worry yet. While the “Pulp Fiction” director confirmed he’d finished penning the script for his final project, he won’t be getting much further with it until his newly opened play, “The Popinjay…
body: He also gave audiences more insight into “The Popinjay Cavalier,” which he said started as a screenplay before the director realized “it really worked as a play.” “I think it will be thrilling,” he said.

Starring Sacha Baron Cohen, “The Popinjay Cavalier” will open at London’s Phoenix Theatre next March, following previews in late Feb. The play, described as a “swashbuckling comedy,” is set to run for three months, closing on June 13. “I’m keen with anticipation to give the West End a great night out,” Tarantino said in a statement when the show was announced.

Tarantino’s most recent release remains “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” which came out in 2019 and starred Brad Pitt, Leonardo DiCaprio, Margot Robbie, Margaret Qualley and more. Pitt won the Oscar for best supporting actor that year, as did Barbara Ling and Nancy Haigh for best production design. Tarantino was also nominated for best picture and best director, while DiCaprio was nominated for best actor.

articles.title: James McAvoy Says ‘Split’ Is The Only Film That ‘Really Consistently Pays Me’
articles.summary: James McAvoy has starred in films including “Speak No Evil,” “Atonement” and “X-Men: First Class,” but he recently revealed the “only” film he still consistently receives residuals from is M.
body: In “Split,” three girls are kidnapped by a man with a diagnosed 23 distinct personalities (McAvoy). “They must try to escape before the apparent emergence of a frightful new 24th,” per the film’s official description. Anya Taylor-Joy, Haley Lu Richardson and Jessica Sula starred alongside McAvoy. The film, which cost just $6 million to make, went on to gross $138.29 million domestically and $140.16 million internationally for a $278.45 million worldwide total.
McAvoy also spoke about Shyamalan and his experience working with the director.

“I very consciously took from many of the directors that I worked with, and subconsciously as well, but the thing I took away from him is his preparedness,” McAvoy said. “He made that film, and [sequel] ‘Glass,’ on incredibly modest budgets, and very focused on how he would maximize his day and maximize his shots and maximize what he got out of the story by just being incredibly well-prepared and being able to share that and communicate that with the crew.”

articles.title: 7 Miles Out review – Carol Morley’s funny-poignant self-portrait of teenage kicks in Stockport
articles.summary: A daring, rich and funny study of the ordeal of having to invent and reinvent your own teenage sense of self amid confounding changes. Carol Morley’s self-portrait of the artist as a young woman is rich, tender and terribly funny and sad: a study in the chaos of being young and a triptych of…
body: 7 Miles Out is based on Morley’s autobiographical novel of the same title, the once-upon-a-time-in-Stockport story of Ann, played with charm and zing by Lucy Halliday, and as a sweetly innocent young girl by Amelie Hughes. Young Ann pretends to be making a radio programme with her cassette recorder the way so many did in the 1970s, and hero-worships her would-be rock journalist elder brother Scott (Kasper Hilton-Hille) – based on Morley’s brother Paul – who is already plugged into the burgeoning post-punk and new wave scene.

Ann’s mum Bryn, wonderfully played by Gemma Whelan, is capable and good-humoured in a no-nonsense sort of way, but later to be beset with anger and mercurial depression. She has however found something to smile about now in the news that her husband and Ann’s dad Ronald, played by Aidan Gillen, has found a prestigious new job in Manchester – seven miles out. So to get to work, he has apparently been supplied with a handsome, though not brand-new car.
points: A daring, rich and funny study of the ordeal of having to invent and reinvent your own teenage sense of self amid confounding changes.

articles.title: Selma Blair ‘did not intend to harm anyone’ during airplane incident, representatives say
articles.summary: Actor experienced a ‘medical emergency’ on flight during which she allegedly injured crew members, statement says. Actor Selma Blair did not mean to hurt anyone during the recent flight which led to her arrest on allegations that she assaulted a pair of cabin crew members, a police officer and a…
body: The lengthy statement also dismissed prior media coverage of Blair’s arrest after a Delta Air Lines flight from Los Angeles to New York as unsympathetic and inaccurate, singling out reporting from several outlets alleging that she tried to open the door of the airplane that she and her fellow passengers were on.
“Selma Blair experienced a medical emergency on the flight,” her representatives’ statement contended. “There was no attempt to open the door of the aircraft. Selma did not intend to harm anyone.”

Friday’s statement from Blair’s camp added some contours to brief remarks made in the days since her arrest by her publicist and lawyer which maintained that there had been a medical emergency but did not elaborate much.

Without specifying who may have done so, the statement on Friday called it “outrageous” for anyone to suggest Blair does not have multiple sclerosis (MS), a chronic neurological disorder which she went public about being diagnosed with in 2018.

articles.title: ‘You can’t make this stuff up’: why we remain fascinated by Elizabeth Holmes
articles.summary: The entrepreneur turned fraudster is the subject of an Oscar-tipped new documentary that takes an unusual look at her strange legacy. David Agus’s first encounter with Elizabeth Holmes at a health conference came as a shock. The Holmes he met in the green room was personable and pleasant.
body: “The accent changed: this deep voice, very serious,” Agus, a medical oncologist, recalls by phone from Los Angeles. “It was as if I had met a person and then interviewed a separate person. That transition from the green room to the stage – I had never experienced something like that before.”

Holmes is not like you or me. She was still a teenager when she founded Theranos, touting technology capable of performing medical tests using only a few drops of blood. She cultivated a distinctive persona: blond hair, an unblinking gaze, a husky voice and a black turtleneck worn in homage to Apple co-founder Steve Jobs.

Holmes mesmerised investors and board members including Rupert Murdoch, Larry Ellison, Carlos Slim and former secretaries of state Henry Kissinger and George Shultz. She became America’s youngest self-made female billionaire. But it was all an illusion, a confidence trick built on a scam. Holmes’s shining career ended in disgrace and imprisonment.

articles.title: Ben Affleck's Canceled Batman Movie Would Have Killed Off A Major DC Comics Hero
articles.summary: Deathstroke actor Joe Manganiello has revealed fresh details about Ben Affleck's canceled DC movie, including which major character would have been killed off.
body: Ben Affleck's "The Batman" remains a holy grail of unmade superhero movies, and the more details that emerge about what could have been, the more tantalizing it sounds. Joe Manganiello, who would've starred in "The Batman" as main villain Slade Wilson/Deathstroke, just dropped one of those details and confirmed a longstanding rumor.

In his new memoir "Bloodlines," Manganiello discusses his role in Affleck's "The Batman." Some of the story details he shares are ones we've known before: that Deathstroke was on a vengeful rampage to destroy Bruce Wayne's life, that the film was inspired by David Fincher's "The Game," and that Barbara Gordon/Batgirl would've appeared. But Manganiello offered some fresh specifics about what Deathstroke's revenge would have looked like, including one casualty of it: Gotham City Police Commissioner Jim Gordon (J.K. Simmons).

articles.title: Off Campus star collaboration 'gave me chills', says Babydoll singer
articles.summary: Jamie Miller hopes he's "doing Wales proud" as his viral hit narrowly misses out on UK number one.
body: The singer behind the TikTok viral hit Babydoll says collaborating with an Off Campus star was "mind-boggling".
Jamie Miller, who is originally from Pontprennau in Cardiff, was close to calling it quits on his music career at the start of 2026, deciding it was his "last chance", financially and emotionally.

But over the summer everything changed when Babydoll caught the attention of people on social media, leading to a viral dance, his first UK top 10 single, and reaching number one in the US iTunes pop chart.
When Miller saw a comment from actor Antonio Cipriano, saying he "needed this song", he sent him a message suggesting he feature on a recording – then "panicked" and added "haha, joking".

articles.title: ‘The Diplomat’ U.K. Prime Minister on the Operatic Way He Learned of His “Shocking” Season 4 Storyline
articles.summary: Showrunner Debora Cahn and actor Rory Kinnear break down the realistic reasons for the Netflix series' latest political shakeup, which plays out amid a surreal episode replete with hallucinations, costumes and an aria.
body: Despite the trippy scenes leading up to Kinnear’s final scene, which comes just one episode after viewers learn that U.K. foreign secretary Austin Dennison (David Gyasi) has died in a helicopter crash, Diplomat showrunner Debora Cahn says there were grounded, real-life reasons for this season’s shake-up in the British government.

“By the time we got to this season, Rory had been prime minister for a period of time where the actual U.K. had like five different people at 10 Downing Street,” Cahn tells The Hollywood Reporter. “And it felt like there was this essential part of being a diplomat, which is that you’re always learning the cast of characters from scratch. You either outlast the people that you’re working with, or you’re sent to a different country. And I wanted to see our team going through the struggle of just when you think you know where the ground is under your feet, it completely changes. You’ve built all these relationships, and suddenly you have nothing.”
Cahn was also interested in showing what it would mean for Keri Russell ‘s American ambassador to the U.K. to no longer have to work with someone like Trowbridge.

articles.title: Why Joe From Street Fighter (2026) Looks So Familiar
articles.summary: The 2026 Street Fighter movie features a fighter called Joe who is a fairly obscure character in the games, but might look familiar to UFC fans.
body: In the annals of "Street Fighter" lore, the character of Joe may be a little obscure. The 2026 "Street Fighter" movie, however, contains a notable role for Joe, and he's played by Australian MMA fighter Alexander Volkanovski. You might be familiar with Volkanovski from his YouTube channel, or any number of his Ultimate Fighting Championship wins.

And just who the heck is Joe? That will take a little bit of looking back. In the original 1987 "Street Fighter" arcade game, you might recall, players took control of either the Japanese martial arts master Ryu or his American rival Ken, and then used clever button-mashing to defeat a string of computer-controlled opponents. One of the fighters in said string was an American karate champ named Joe. He was a boring blond guy with red pants and not much personality otherwise.
